newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lupin disease in Australia spreads interstate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lupin disease in Australia spreads interstate.

text.p: Anthracnose, a fungal disease which broke out in Western Australia's (WA) albus (white) lupin crops in early September, had recently been confirmed in New South Wales (NSW) after earlier being also found in South Australia (SA), chairman of the NSW Farmers' Association grains committee, Xavier Martin, said on Monday.
After its discovery in WA, anthracnose spread to the Eyre Peninsula in SA and had recently been confirmed in ornamental lupins in gardens in southern NSW, he said in a statement.
Martin called for an urgent change to regulations governing the import of lupins and lupin seeds to ensure that proper inspections occur and substantial penalties apply to illegal imports.

The statement followed a recent forecast by the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics that Australian lupin production would fall by 14 percent to slightly more than 1.2 million tonnes in 1996/97, mainly the result of lower production in WA which accounts for 85 percent of Australia's lupin production.
Thousands of hectares have been ploughed in in WA after anthracnose was discovered in the state's A$200 million lupin crop, which is mainly used as stock feed.
Australia is one of only two countries previously free of the fungus disease which reduces lupin yields by 50 to 60 percent.
"Australian grain growers feared the spread of anthracnose in lupin crops," Martin said.
